speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To better understand what's happening, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the fluctuation in strength and specific eye movements are very helpful clues. Given your symptoms, I need to check if you experience muscle weakness in the face or have difficulty swallowing. Also, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids lately?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Study. Also, do you experience any difficulty swallowing or chewing?
